Why this one: The standard one, everyone knows it, reasoners built in. I use it to check the reasoner is happy and to grab the class hierarchy screenshot

Why this one: Diffs cleanly so I can see what changed. It's also what other people download

Why this one: Search before you invent. This one habit is what separates an ontology that looks amateur from one that doesn't

Why this one: THE most important decision here. The mapping is a file I can put in the appendix, a reviewer can read it, and rerunning it after I fix the data takes one command. TOXIN did exactly this in an Oxford journal
What I said no to: A Python script. Same triples, but nobody can audit it and I can't cite it. OntoRefine is good but traps the mapping inside GraphDB

Why this one: Turns the mapping into readable documentation with diagrams. Free appendix material
Reasoning built in, and a visual explorer that draws the graph. Showing a supervisor a picture beats any paragraph I could write
What I said no to: Jena Fuseki is simpler but its reasoning is weak. Stardog is stronger but you have to pay

Why this one: Comes with Protégé, solid, fast enough
What I said no to: Pellet and ELK. But careful: if I write SWRL rules HermiT ignores them SILENTLY, so I'd have to switch

What I picked: Openllet, only if I need it
Why this one: Handles SWRL, which HermiT doesn't. OntoCosmetic used SWRL for exactly this kind of rule
What I said no to: Writing everything as rules. It slows reasoning right down

Why this one: OWL can't say 'every product MUST have a brand', because it assumes anything unsaid might just be unknown. SHACL can. This is where validate_dataset.py moves to
What I said no to: Trusting the reasoner to catch bad data. Wrong tool, and it'll quietly accept rubbish

Why this one: 41 known design mistakes, graded. One afternoon for a real evaluation number that none of our competitors has
What I said no to: Not evaluating the design at all, which is what 28 out of 28 reviewed studies did

Why this one: 24 checks on whether people can find and reuse it. Since I criticise everyone for not publishing, I'd better measure my own
What I said no to: Just claiming it's FAIR without measuring

Why this one: Depth, breadth, richness. Gives me comparable numbers for the evaluation table
What I said no to: Reporting just a class count and hoping

What I said no to: Writing docs by hand and watching them go stale
